title: UPSC CSE - Indian Economy - BoP, CAD Currency Exchange
subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. A share of the household financial savings goes towards government borrowings.
2. Dated securities issued at market-related rates in auctions form a large component of internal debt.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. Household financial savings contribute to government borrowings, and dated securities issued at market-related rates form a large component of internal debt.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: With reference to the expenditure made by an organization or a company, which of the following statements is/are correct?\n1. Acquiring new technology is capital expenditure.\n2. Debt financing is considered capital expenditure, while equity financing is considered revenue expenditure.
questions.explain: Acquiring new technology is considered capital expenditure as it will generate profit in the future and helps in the creation of new assets. However, both debt financing and equity financing are generally considered capital expenditure.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to the Indian economy, consider the following statements:
1. An increase in Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) indicates the appreciation of rupee.
2. An increase in the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER) indicates an improvement in trade competitiveness.
3. An increasing trend in domestic inflation relative to inflation in other countries is likely to cause an increasing divergence between NEER and REER.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: An increase in NEER indicates appreciation of the rupee. Statement 2 is incorrect: An increase in REER indicates a decrease in trade competitiveness. Statement 3 is correct: Increasing domestic inflation relative to other countries is likely to cause divergence between NEER and REER.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tight monetary policy of the US Federal Reserve could lead to capital flight.
2. Capital flight may increase the interest cost of firms with existing External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs).
3. Devaluation of domestic currency decreases the currency risk associated with ECBs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: UPSC has dropped this question.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The effect of devaluation of a currency is that it necessarily
1. improves the competitiveness of the domestic exports in the foreign markets
2. increases the foreign value of domestic currency
3. improves the trade balance
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Devaluation improves the competitiveness of domestic exports. Statement 2 is incorrect: Devaluation decreases the foreign value of domestic currency. Statement 3 is not necessarily correct: Devaluation may improve exports but also increase import costs, so trade balance improvement is not guaranteed.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Foreign currency convertible bonds
2. Foreign institutional investment with certain conditions
3. Global depository receipts
4. Non-resident external deposits
Which of the above can be included in Foreign Direct Investments?
questions.explain: Foreign currency convertible bonds, foreign institutional investment with certain conditions, and global depository receipts are considered as part of FDI. Non-resident external deposits are not included in FDI.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The value of Indo-Sri Lanka trade has consistently increased in the last decade.
2. Textile and textile articles constitute an important item of the trade between India and Bangladesh.
3. In the last five years, Nepal has been the largest trading partner of India in South Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is incorrect: Indo-Sri Lanka trade has not consistently increased. Statement 2 is correct: Textiles are an important trade item between India and Bangladesh. Statement 3 is incorrect: Bangladesh, not Nepal, has been India's largest trading partner in South Asia.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Term 'West Texas Intermediate', sometimes found in news, refers to a grade of
questions.explain: West Texas Intermediate is a particular grade of crude oil. It is primarily sourced from Texas and serves as a global benchmark for setting oil prices.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: With reference to Foreign Direct Investment in India, which one of the following is considered its major characteristic? (2020)
options: It is the investment through capital instruments essentially in a listed company.
It is largely non-debt, creating capital flow.
It is an investment which involves debt-servicing.
It is the instrument made by foreign institutional investors in the Government securities.
questions.explain: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is a type of investment where an investor based in one country invests in another country. FDI equity inflows do not create any debt and are non-volatile. Hence, these are largely non-debt creating capital flow and their returns depend on the performance of the projects financed by the foreign investors.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Gold Tranche (Reserve Tranche) refers to (2020)
options: a loan system of the World Bank
one of the operations of a Central Bank
a credit system granted by WTO to its members
a credit system granted by IMF to its members
questions.explain: Reserve Tranche is the component of a member country's quota with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), that is, in the form of gold or foreign currency. It is a credit system granted by the IMF to its members. For any member country, out of the total quota, 25% should be paid in the form of foreign currency or gold. Hence, this is called a Reserve Tranche or Gold Tranche.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
If another global financial crisis happens in the near future, which of the following actions/policies are most likely to give some immunity to India? (2020)
1. Not depending on the short-term foreign borrowings
2. Opening up to more foreign banks
3. Maintaining full capital account convertibility
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Not depending on short-term foreign borrowings will provide immunity to India during a global financial crisis. Opening up to more foreign banks would be risky as there is a high chance of banks becoming inefficient in NPA recovery. Maintaining full capital account convertibility during a crisis would also be risky.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Among the following, which one is the largest exporter of rice in the world in the last five years? (2019)
questions.explain: India is the largest rice exporter with a significant market share. In the last few years, India topped the list of rice exporting countries, followed by Thailand, which stood second in the list.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Among the agricultural commodities imported by India, which one of the following accounts for the highest imports in terms of value in the last five years? (2019)
questions.explain: Amongst the mentioned agricultural commodities, Vegetable Oils constitute the highest imports in terms of value in the last five years. Vegetable Oil imports have been a cause for concern, as the country depends on imports for meeting roughly 60% of its domestic demand.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: (2019)
1. Most of India's external debt is owed by governmental entities.
2. All of India's external debt is denominated in US dollars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are incorrect. Commercial borrowings remained the largest component of external debt, not governmental entities. US dollar denominated debt remained the largest component of India's external debt at 53.9%, not all of it.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
In the context of India, which of the following factors is/are contributor/ contributors to reducing the risk of a currency crisis? (2019)
1. The foreign currency earnings of India's IT sector
2. Increasing government expenditure
3. Remittances from Indians abroad
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Foreign currency earnings of India's IT sector and remittances from Indians abroad increase forex reserves, helping reduce the risk of a currency crisis. Increasing government expenditure is not directly related to reducing currency crisis risk.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following is not the most likely measure the Government/RBI takes to stop the slide of the Indian rupee? (2019)
options: Curbing imports of non-essential goods and promoting exports
Encouraging Indian borrowers to issue rupee denominated Masala Bonds
Easing conditions relating to external commercial borrowing
questions.explain: An expansionary monetary policy is not the most likely measure to stop the sliding of Indian rupee, as it can cause the rupee to slide more. It increases money supply, reduces interest rates, potentially leading to outflow of foreign investments and further depreciation of the rupee.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: (2019)
1. Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) exchange rates are calculated by comparing the prices of the same basket of goods and services in different countries.
2. In terms of PPP dollars, India is the sixth largest economy in the world.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: PPP exchange rate is calculated by comparing prices of a similar basket of goods and services in different countries. Statement 2 is incorrect: In terms of PPP dollars, India is the third largest economy in the world (fourth if the European Union is considered as a common economic space).
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements: (2018)
1. The quantity of imported edible oils is more than the domestic production of edible oils in the last five years.
2. The Government does not impose any customs duty on all the imported edible oils as a special case.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: The quantity of imported edible oils is more than domestic production in the last five years. India depends on imports for around 70% of its domestic demand. Statement 2 is incorrect: The government levies 35% and 45% import duty on all crude and refined edible oils respectively.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee Report has recommended a debt to GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023, comprising 40% for the Central Government and 20% for the State Governments.
2. The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments.
3. As per the Constitution of India, it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the former owes any outstanding liabilities to the latter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: The FRBM review committee in its 2017 report recommended bringing down the debt to GDP ratio for both Centre and States combined to 60 percent (40% for centre and 20% for states) by 2023.

Statement 2 is not correct: At the time of the report submission, domestic liabilities of the Central Government accounted for 46.5% of GDP and that of States accounted for 24% of GDP.

Statement 3 is correct: Article 293(3) of the Constitution states that a State may not raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India if there is still outstanding any part of a loan made to the State by the Government of India.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tax revenue as a per cent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
2. The fiscal deficit as a per cent of GDP of India has steadily increased in the last decade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Tax revenue as a percentage of GDP has not steadily increased in the last decade. There has been a rise and fall without following a fixed pattern.\n\nStatement 2 is not correct: Fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP has not steadily increased in the last decade. There has been a rise and fall with no steady pattern of rising or falling.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are included in the capital budget of the Government of India?
1. Expenditure on acquisition of assets like roads, buildings, machinery, etc.
2. Loans received from foreign governments
3. Loans and advances granted to the States and Union Territories
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain:
The Capital Budget consists of capital receipts and payments. All three given options are included in the Capital Budget.
1. Expenditure on acquisition of assets is capital expenditure.
2. Loans from foreign governments are capital receipts.
3. Loans given to states/UTs are capital expenditure as they add to government assets.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which action/actions of the following can be taken by the government to reduce the deficit?
1. Reducing revenue expenditure
2. Introducing new welfare schemes
3. Rationalizing subsidies
4. Reducing import duty
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain:
To reduce budget deficit:
1. Reducing revenue expenditure will help reduce deficit.
2. New welfare schemes will increase expenditure and deficit.
3. Rationalizing subsidies will reduce expenditure and deficit.
4. Reducing import duties will reduce government revenue and increase deficit.
Therefore, only 1 and 3 will help reduce the deficit.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
What is/are the purpose/purposes of the Government's 'Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme' and 'Gold Monetization Scheme'?
1. To bring the idle gold lying with Indian households into the economy
2. To promote FDI in the gold and jewellery sector
3. To reduce India's dependence on gold imports
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain:
The Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme and Gold Monetization Scheme aim to:
1. Bring idle gold held by households into the economy (correct)
2. They are not concerned with increasing FDI in gold/jewellery sector (incorrect)
3. Reduce India's dependence on gold imports by utilizing domestic idle gold and providing an alternative investment to physical gold (correct)
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Recently, which one of the following currencies has been proposed to be added to the basket of IMF's SDR?
questions.explain: In 2016, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) added the Chinese Renminbi (RMB) to the basket of currencies that make up the Special Drawing Right (SDR).
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the term 'import cover', sometimes seen in the news?
options: It is the ratio of value of imports to the Gross Domestic Product of a country
It is the total value of imports of a country in a year
It is the ratio between the value of exports and that of imports between two countries
It is the number of months of imports that could be paid for by a country's international reserves
questions.explain: 'Import Cover' refers to the number of months over which a country can pay for its imports from its International Reserves. It is a traditional trade-based indicator of reserve adequacy, defined as the number of months of import equivalent to reserves.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: The problem of international liquidity is related to the non-availability of:
questions.explain: International Liquidity primarily refers to the resources available to countries to tackle Balance of Payments deficits. Modern global trading systems depend on dollars and other global currencies (hard currencies) like Yen, Euro, Pound, etc. These currencies account for major proportions of every country's Balance of Payments. Hence, the non-availability of them leads to a problem of international liquidity.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Convertibility of rupee implies:
options: being able to convert rupee notes into gold
allowing the value of rupee to be fixed by market forces
freely permitting the conversion of rupee to other currencies and vice versa
developing an international market for currencies in India
questions.explain: Convertibility of rupee means that rupee can be freely converted into other currencies for various purposes and vice versa. It can be understood from two aspects:\n1. Current Account Convertibility: Rupee can be freely converted for trade purposes (imports/exports). India allows this.\n2. Capital Account Convertibility: Rupee can be freely converted for capital transactions. India does not fully allow this.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
There has been a persistent deficit budget year after year. Which of the following actions can be taken by the government to reduce the deficit?
1. Reducing revenue expenditure
2. Introducing new welfare schemes
3. Rationalizing subsidies
4. Expanding industries
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain:
To reduce budget deficit:
1. Reducing revenue expenditure will help reduce deficit (correct)
2. New welfare schemes will increase expenditure and deficit (incorrect)
3. Rationalizing subsidies will reduce expenditure and deficit (correct)
4. Expanding industries will increase expenditure and deficit (incorrect)
Therefore, only 1 and 3 will help reduce the deficit.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: With reference to the Fourteenth Finance Commission, which of the following statements is/are correct?\n1. It has increased the share of States in the central divisible pool from 32 percent to 42 percent.\n2. It has made recommendations concerning sector-specific grants.
questions.explain: The 14th Finance Commission considerably increased the devolution of taxes from the Centre to states from 32 percent to 42 percent. The Commission had recommended that tax devolution should be the primary source of transfer of funds to states. This would increase the flow of unconditional transfers and give states more flexibility in their spending. It has not made any recommendations concerning sector-specific grants.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to the Union Budget, which of the following is/are covered under Non-Plan Expenditure?
1. Defence Expenditure
2. Interest Payments
3. Salaries and pensions
4. Subsidies
questions.explain: Non-plan expenditure constitutes the dominant portion of budget expenditure. These expenses are spread across defence, interest payments for debt, subsidies (especially for food and fertilizers) and salaries and pensions of employees in various government services.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to Balance of Payments, which of the following constitutes/constitute the Current Account?
1. Balance of Trade
2. Foreign Assets
3. Balance of Invisibles
4. Special Drawing Rights
questions.explain: With reference to Balance of Payments, the Current Account constitutes Balance of Trade and Balance of Invisibles. Balance of Trade is the difference between a country's Imports and Exports. Balance of Invisibles is the difference between a country's Service Imports and Service Exports.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: The Balance of Payments of a country is a systematic record of
options: all import and export transactions of a country during a given period of time, normally a year
goods exported from a country during a year
economic transaction between the government of one country to another
capital movements from one country to another
questions.explain: The Balance of Payments is a record of all transactions conducted between a country and the rest of the world. It keeps a systematic record of all imports and exports of goods/services/capital and other factors and transfer payments generally during the span of a year.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Which of the following constitute Capital Account?
1. Foreign Loans
2. Foreign Direct Investment
3. Private Remittances
4. Portfolio Investment
questions.explain: Foreign Loans, Foreign Direct Investment and Portfolio Investment form a component of the Capital Account as they are adding up to the existing liabilities of the country as they warrant a future repayment liability. Private remittance is a part of the current account.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of items is included in India's foreign-exchange reserves?
options: Foreign-currency assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) and loans from foreign countries
Foreign-currency assets, gold holdings of the RBI and SDRs
Foreign-currency assets, loans from the World Bank and SDRs
Foreign-currency assets, gold holdings of the RBI and loans from the World Bank
questions.explain: Forex reserves in the Indian context consist of foreign currencies, holdings of gold by the RBI and Special Drawing Rights with the International Monetary Fund which are foreign exchange reserve assets created and maintained by the RBI.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The price of any currency in international market is decided by the
1. World Bank
2. demand for goods/services provided by the country concerned
3. stability of the government of the concerned country
4. economic potential of the country in question
questions.explain: The price of any currency in the international market can be determined at floating rate based on demand and supply. Demand for goods/services provided by the country concerned directly impacts the demand or supply for that country's currency impacting the exchange rates. Stability of the government provides greater trust and acceptability of that nation's currency. The World Bank and economic potential don't directly determine currency prices.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Which of the following would include Foreign Direct Investment in India?
1. Subsidiaries of companies in India
2. Majority foreign equity holding in Indian companies
3. Companies exclusively financed by foreign companies
4. Portfolio investment
questions.explain: Foreign direct investments can be made by opening subsidiaries in India, holding majority equity in Indian companies, or companies exclusively financed by foreign companies. Portfolio investment is not considered FDI.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: In terms of economy, the visit by foreign nationals to witness the XIX Commonwealth Games in India amounted to
questions.explain: The hosting of global events brings foreign nationals into the country. They consume goods and services in India, exchanging foreign currency for Rupees. This amounts to the export of goods and services from India to foreign nationals, even though the consumption happens within India.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Why is the Government of India disinvesting its equity in the Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)?\n1. The Government intends to use the revenue earned from the disinvestment mainly to pay back the external debt.\n2. The Government no longer intends to retain the management control of the CPSEs.
questions.explain: The revenue earned from disinvestment is not intended to be used for paying back external debt, instead it is used for creating other social value creating assets. Disinvestment may not necessarily mean that the government is letting go the management control in CPSEs, instead the Government may choose to sell only a minority stake and keep managerial control in its hands.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following statements appropriately describes the fiscal stimulus?
options: It is a massive investment by the Government in the manufacturing sector to ensure the supply of goods to meet demand surge caused by rapid economic growth.
It is an intense affirmative action of the Government to boost economic activity in the country.
It is the Government's intensive action on financial institutions to ensure disbursement of loans to agriculture and allied sectors to promote greater food production and contain food inflation.
It is an extreme affirmative action by the government to pursue its policy of financial inclusion.
questions.explain: Fiscal Stimulus is the process of infusing money into an economy that is going through a crisis. It is an intense affirmative action of the government to boost economic activity in the country. During an economic downturn, the government implements measures to reinvigorate the economy, often involving increased spending to boost employment and demand, and reducing taxes to increase money supply in the market. It is generally not limited to or specific to a particular sector.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q: Both Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) are related to investment in a country. Which of the following statements best represents an important difference between the two?
options: FII helps bring better management skills and technology, while FDI only brings in capital.
FII helps in increasing capital availability in general, while FDI only targets specific sectors.
FDI flows only into the secondary market, while FII targets the primary market.
FII is considered to be more stable than FDI.
questions.explain: FII helps in increasing the general capital availability in the country as they invest large sums of money into varied asset classes across the domestic markets. On the contrary, FDI is targeted only at a particular sector and at times only to a particular business entity. FDI involves establishing long-lasting business interests, while FII primarily focuses on short-term investments in income-generating assets like stocks and bonds.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following action which the Government can take:
1. Devaluing the domestic currency.
2. Reduction in export subsidy.
3. Adopting suitable policies which attract greater FDI and more funds from FIIs.

Which of the following action/actions can help in reducing the Current Account Deficit?
questions.explain: Devaluing the domestic currency will make Indian goods cheaper, increasing exports. Reduction in export subsidy will make exports more expensive, increasing the Current Account deficit. Attracting greater FDI and FII will increase foreign exchange inflow. Both devaluation and attracting foreign investment will help reduce the Current Account Deficit.
questions.subject: Indian Economy

questions.q:
With reference to the Tea Board in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Tea Board is a statutory body.
2. It is a regulatory body attached to the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
3. The Tea Board's Head Office is situated in Bengaluru.
4. The Board has overseas offices at Dubai and Moscow.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The Tea Board of India is a statutory body functioning under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It was set up under the Tea Act of 1953. Its Head Office is situated in Kolkata, not Bengaluru. The Tea Board has overseas offices in Moscow, Dubai, Hamburg, London and New York.
questions.subject: Indian Economy
